_comment: Roster overrides for the season projection engine.
Copy to rosters/team_assignments_<target_year>.json and edit. This file
expresses everything player history cannot: offseason signings, trades,
retirements, and manual corrections. Without it, a player's target team is
inferred from his most recent playing time, so every offseason move is
wrong until the next season's data exists.
An override changes team context for BOTH clubs: the player leaves one
roster aggregate and joins another, so both teams' bottom-up run
environments are recomputed, and every hitter on both teams has his R/RBI
rescaled accordingly.
Fields per entry:
player_id  (required) MLBAM player id, matching PlayerId in out/*.csv
team       any code or full name canonical_team() understands --
'SF', 'NY-A', 'CHW', 'New York Yankees'. Two special values:
'FA'  an unsigned FREE AGENT. He keeps a full rate line and
can be given playing time and a role, because he will
sign somewhere -- we just don't know where yet. He is
excluded from every team aggregate so he cannot act
as a 31st club.
null  team genuinely unknown (unlinked id, bad data). Not
the same as a free agent; provenance is missing.
Use null only for real ignorance, and 'FA' whenever you know
the player is simply unsigned.
team_id    alternative to 'team': an explicit MLBAM team id.
note       free text, ignored by the loader. Record the transaction and
its date here.
Unresolvable teams and entries with no usable player_id are skipped with a
warning rather than failing the run.

assignments.note: EXAMPLE ONLY -- Aaron Judge did not sign with San Francisco. Delete this block.
EXAMPLE ONLY -- shows the explicit team_id form (147 = NYY). Delete this block.
EXAMPLE ONLY -- an unsigned free agent. He keeps his rate line and can be given playing time; he just has no club yet. Delete this block.
EXAMPLE ONLY -- team genuinely unknown, which is NOT the same as 'FA'. Delete this block.

_reserves_comment: Playing time each club is holding back for a signing it has not made yet.
Without this, the allocator spreads the full ~6,150 PA / ~1,458 IP across
the players currently on hand, so every incumbent absorbs the plate
appearances that will actually go to the free agent -- the whole roster is
over-projected. Reserving a share leaves the club deliberately UNDER-
projected instead, which is the honest state of a team mid-offseason.
team / team_id  which club (same vocabulary as assignments above)
pa_share        fraction of the hitter PA budget held back, 0 to 0.5
ip_share        fraction of the pitcher IP budget held back, 0 to 0.5
Hitters and pitchers reserve independently -- a club shopping for a
starter is not necessarily shopping for a bat. Reserves are the
counterpart to the 'FA' assignments above: the free agents hold the
playing time, the reserves hold the space for them, and the two should
A reserve says 'this club's playing time is not all accounted for'. It does
NOT say 'this club is better than its roster looks' -- the quality of a
player nobody has signed is unknowable, so reserves never touch the rate
